newsitem.title: UK: Regulator against Centrica windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: Regulator against Centrica windfall tax.

text.p: Industry regulator Ofgas said on Wednesday gas supplier Centrica, recently demerged from British Gas, should be exempted from any windfall taxes on utilities.
The opposition Labour party has said it would introduce such taxes if it would come to power after the May 1 election.
Labour has declined to say exactly which utilities would be affected and to what extent, but industry analysts speculate Centrica might have to pay up to 150 million stg.
But Ofgas believes Centrica does not deserve a windfall tax because it operates in an increasingly competitive market, a regulator spokesman said.
The British domestic gas supply market is in the process of being opened up to rivals with competition already introduced in the south of England.
The market for industrial users was already liberalised in the early 1990s, leaving former monopoly Centrica with a market share of about 35 percent.
Centrica, which was spun off from British Gas in February, has already said it did not expect to earn enough money to pay-out dividends in the near future.
Ofgas would not say what it stance would be on any windfall taxes for the British Gas rump, which has been re-named BG Plc.
The Ofgas spokesman said the regulator's stance depended on the outcome of an ongoing enquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
The MMC is investigating Ofgas proposals for a tougher price regime for BG's gas transport operations in Britain.
The proposals have been vetted by the MMC since October when BG said they were unacceptable, claiming the proposals would trim cash flow by about 400 million stg a year.
